searchText: > Other stuff require validation as well (notice 400 responses). <@!545555441518772225> the docs say: "Submits Attestation object to node. If attestation passes all validation constraints, node MUST publish attestation on appropriate subnet." vs "The beacon node is not required to validate the signed BeaconBlock, and a successful response (20X) only indicates that the broadcast has been successful. " taking a look at `/eth/v1/node/syncing` at the moment, and the term `head_slot` is interesting. from the description it does sound like basically the calculated head slot of the network, vs. the last slot where a block got created (ethstats column 'head slot' is the last block). Am i correct that `head_slot` in the syncing response is the current calculated slot? concrete example: slot1: block, slot2: empty, slot3: empty should i report back that `head_slot` is slot1 like ethstats, or should i report that we're at slot3? hopefully this better describes the syncing endpoint question i have: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-APIs/issues/77 > <@!545555441518772225> the docs say: > > "Submits Attestation object to node. If attestation passes all validation constraints, node MUST publish attestation on appropriate subnet." > > vs > > "The beacon node is not required to validate the signed BeaconBlock, and a successful response (20X) only indicates that the broadcast has been successful. " <@!361447803194441738> Seems like that description is from <@!535705896224030720> original proposal. I'm pretty sure that we need to validate block anyways. Also we could list all invalid block/attestation/etc errors you check and add those to the spec if you are up for it? You definitely will need to validate the block eventually. The question is whether you need to take the hit on timing to validate it before broadcast How "trusted" is the VC If i had a VC connected to two BNs and I got a block to sign from one of them and wanted to broadcast via both, I'd prefer no validation on the BN that didnt originally produce the block for fast network dissemination But the BN is taking on peer score risk depending on the behaviour of the validator > If i had a VC connected to two BNs and I got a block to sign from one of them and wanted to broadcast via both, I'd prefer no validation on the BN that didnt originally produce the block for fast network dissemination <@!291925846556540928> are you suggesting flag for validator to signal BN if block should be validated? that wouldn't help! the problem is the BN trsuting the VC so a flag from the validator can't be trusted if you can't trust hte VC I'm inclined to have a strong trust relationship assumed in the base API and if instead you were a service provider, to have strong authenication and to add things like "only broadcast blocks, the BN previously handed out to be signed" > I'm inclined to have a strong trust relationship assumed in the base API <@!291925846556540928> I'd rather the BN didn't assume trust, in that it verified all data coming in to it from both P2P and API. It's a more solid basis on which to build, IMO. If the API is considered "trusted" but the P2P connections aren't, it doesn't seem to be a major benefit to the network as a whole for the block received via API to not be validated, but for the block received via P2P to have to be. Seems like we're not gaining a lot in terms of speed of transmissions (no verification prior to first hop) and, as you say, opening up the beacon node to being dinged on its score.

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
> Other stuff require validation as well (notice 400 responses).
<@!545555441518772225> the docs say:

"Submits Attestation object to node. If attestation passes all validation constraints, node MUST publish attestation on appropriate subnet."

vs

"The beacon node is not required to validate the signed BeaconBlock, and a successful response (20X) only indicates that the broadcast has been successful. "

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content:
taking a look at `/eth/v1/node/syncing` at the moment, and the term `head_slot` is interesting. from the description it does sound like basically the calculated head slot of the network, vs. the last slot where a block got created (ethstats column 'head slot' is the last block).
Am i correct that `head_slot` in the syncing response is the current calculated slot?
concrete example: slot1: block, slot2: empty, slot3: empty
should i report back that `head_slot` is slot1 like ethstats, or should i report that we're at slot3?

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: hopefully this better describes the syncing endpoint question i have: https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-APIs/issues/77

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content:
> <@!545555441518772225> the docs say:
> 
> "Submits Attestation object to node. If attestation passes all validation constraints, node MUST publish attestation on appropriate subnet."
> 
> vs
> 
> "The beacon node is not required to validate the signed BeaconBlock, and a successful response (20X) only indicates that the broadcast has been successful. "
<@!361447803194441738> Seems like that description is from <@!535705896224030720> original proposal. I'm pretty sure that we need to validate block anyways. Also we could list all invalid block/attestation/etc errors you check and add those to the spec if you are up for it?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: You definitely will need to validate the block eventually. The question is whether you need to take the hit on timing to validate it before broadcast

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: If i had a VC connected to two BNs and I got a block to sign from one of them and wanted to broadcast via both, I'd prefer no validation on the BN that didnt originally produce the block for fast network dissemination

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: But the BN is taking on peer score risk depending on the behaviour of the validator

excerpts.author: mpetrunic
excerpts.content:
> If i had a VC connected to two BNs and I got a block to sign from one of them and wanted to broadcast via both, I'd prefer no validation on the BN that didnt originally produce the block for fast network dissemination
<@!291925846556540928> are you suggesting flag for validator to signal BN if block should be validated?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: that wouldn't help! the problem is the BN trsuting the VC so a flag from the validator can't be trusted if you can't trust hte VC

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I'm inclined to have a strong trust relationship assumed in the base API

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: and if instead you were a service provider, to have strong authenication and to add things like "only broadcast blocks, the BN previously handed out to be signed"

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
> I'm inclined to have a strong trust relationship assumed in the base API
<@!291925846556540928> I'd rather the BN didn't assume trust, in that it verified all data coming in to it from both P2P and API.  It's a more solid basis on which to build, IMO.

If the API is considered "trusted" but the P2P connections aren't, it doesn't seem to be a major benefit to the network as a whole for the block received via API to not be validated, but for the block received via P2P to have to be.  Seems like we're not gaining a lot in terms of speed of transmissions (no verification prior to first hop) and, as you say, opening up the beacon node to being dinged on its score.
